title: Adaptive initiative gating and playbook for error budget fractionation
creator: Lydia Park
description:
Background:
Redwood teams currently manage error budgets and SLOs via disparate dashboards and manual playbooks. When an initiative consumes error budget quickly, we lack a standardized, automated way to gate rollout velocity, notify stakeholders, and adjust initiative weights across teams. This ticket proposes an "adaptive initiative gating" capability that fractions error budgets across active initiatives, projects burn-rate forecasts, and enforces gated rollout actions when threshold conditions meet policy.

Goals:
- Provide a single product-backed playbook for initiative-level error budget fractionation and automated gating.
- Surface burn-rate forecasts and time-to-breach projections per initiative and service.
- Add console UI and API to configure per-initiative gating policies, desired rollback actions, and notification routing.
- Integrate with rollout system to throttle/rollback canaries when initiative-level SLI trajectories exceed thresholds.
- Create acceptance testing and runbook templates so on-call and PMs can act consistently.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Fractionation model: allocate a portion of a service error budget to each active initiative based on configurable weights (team priority, customer impact, SLA tier). We keep a global initiative allocation ledger and expose both absolute and percentage allocations.
2) Burn-rate projection: compute rolling burn-rate over windows (5m, 1h, 6h), forecast time-to-breach at current trajectory, and compute confidence intervals using recent variance.
3) Policy engine: allow policies that map burn-rate/time-to-breach to actions: alert, pause rollout, reduce traffic %, immediate rollback. Policies can be per-initiative or inherited from service defaults.
4) Automated gating: wire policy engine to rollout controller (canary/A-B) so that actions can be executed automatically or require manual approval, depending on policy.
5) Console UX: initiative detail page with allocation, burn-rate chart, projected breach timeline, policy editor, and one-click runbook actions. Global Reliability hub to list initiatives sorted by urgency and aggregated error budget runway.
6) API & infra: expose endpoints to read/write initiative allocations and policy; emit structured events for auditing. Integrate with existing SLO telemetry pipeline and Slack/pager routing.

Telemetry & Metrics to produce:
- initiative_error_budget_remaining (percent)
- initiative_burn_rate (tokens per minute normalized)
- initiative_time_to_breach (minutes)
- initiative_policy_actions_count (per policy, per day)
- gating_actions_executed (automated vs manual)

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0: experiment with two pilot services and 3 initiatives each; gather feedback (2 weeks).
- Phase 1: public beta for Reliability org with UI and a limited set of policies (4 weeks).
- Phase 2: GA for all customers with API and audit logs (8 weeks).

Risks & mitigation:
- False positives causing unnecessary rollbacks: provide a manual approval mode, confidence thresholds, and quick-undo button.
- Overly complex policy surface: ship with a small set of recommended policy templates and guardrails.
- Telemetry lag undermining gating accuracy: require an explicit freshness SLA for SLO feed; block automation if data staleness > 2x window.

Acceptance criteria (see list below) and clear owner responsibilities are included. Links: PRD (confluence) - https://confluence.redwood.ai/reliability/initiative-fractionation-prd, design spec - https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/initiative-gating-v1, demo dashboard prototype - internal:dashboards/reliability/hub/pilot
acceptance_criteria: Console shows per-initiative error budget allocation and remaining percentage for pilot services
Burn-rate projection UI renders 5m/1h/6h windows and time-to-breach forecasts with confidence band
Product policy editor can create a policy that, when matched, pauses a canary deployment via rollout controller (manual or automatic mode)
API endpoints exist to read/write initiative allocations and retrieve current burn-rate metrics
Audit log entries emitted for every gating decision with initiative ID, policy ID, actor (system or user), and timestamp
Runbook template available and validated by on-call during pilot (post-mortem drill simulated)
